name: Abū Muḥammad Salama ibn ʿĀṣim al-Naḥwī
summary: Kufan grammarian, the transmitter of al-Farrāʾ's books and teacher of Thaʿlab; trustworthy and learned, in Ibn al-Anbārī's words.
bio: Salama learned from al-Farrāʾ and transmitted his books, and Thaʿlab learned from him; Ibn al-Anbārī calls him trustworthy, reliable and learned.
Al-Zubaydī counts him in the fourth generation of the grammarians of Kufa, the companions of al-Farrāʾ; the fifth generation, Thaʿlab's, he calls 'the companions of Salama'.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 204–205
